problem:
What is the standard deviation of the following data set?

$$
1,\,1,\,5,\,4,\,9
$$

feedback.problem:
Compute the standard deviation $\sigma $ of the following data set:

$$
-9,\,-7,\,1,\,3,\,4
$$

Do not round your answer.

$\sigma =$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a data set ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is the square root of the variance:

$$
\sigma =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2}}=\sqrt{\,\,\,\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-{(\overset{―}{x})}^{2}}
$$

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-9-7+1+3+4) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (-8) \\  & =-\frac{8}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [(-9)^{2}+(-7)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot [81+49+1+9+16] \\  & =\frac{156}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{156}{5}-{(-\frac{8}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{156}{5}-\frac{64}{25} \\  & =\frac{780-64}{25} \\  & =\frac{716}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the standard deviation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\sigma  & =\sqrt{{\sigma }^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{716}{25}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{179}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
